strengths: Novel representation-space approach to lifelong knowledge editing for unstructured knowledge, with two well-motivated geometric properties (semantic locality and semantic alignment) empirically validated through comprehensive analysis

Strong and consistent empirical results across multiple models and datasets, maintaining stable performance at 1,000 sequential edits while baselines degrade (0.963 BertScore vs. 0.673 for WISE on UnKE), with superior paraphrase generalization and MMLU preservation

Comprehensive method design flowing logically from identified properties: consistency-robust training for generalization, query-adaptive routing for lifelong control, and shared-subspace interventions for memory efficiency (~70% storage savings)

Extensive ablations and analysis including editing distance validation of Prop. 2 (91/100 cases), hyperparameter sensitivity studies, scalability analysis at 1,500 items with >95% routing accuracy, and case studies demonstrating advantages over collapsed baselines
Practical efficiency with 50% memory reduction vs. UnKE baselines and negligible inference latency overhead while maintaining competitive performance across ZsRE structured editing task
weaknesses: Limited theoretical justification beyond empirical validation: Properties 1-2 are observed but lack formal explanation; first-order Taylor approximation validity and error bounds in Sec. 4.1 are not analyzed; no formal router correctness analysis

Experimental design concerns that warrant investigation: extremely low temperature (0.001) fundamentally changes task difficulty vs. realistic settings—sensitivity analysis critical but missing; EditEverything paraphrases generated by Gemini introducing potential distribution shift; unclear if baselines evaluated on same synthetic paraphrases

Routing mechanism has unanalyzed failure modes: hardcoded threshold τ_sim=0.9 with limited justification; O(m) lookup cost becomes problematic at scale; no analysis of when nearest-neighbor assumption breaks down in crowded representation spaces; missing error case analysis

Clustering strategy is somewhat ad-hoc: hierarchical agglomerative clustering with recursive refinement lacks theoretical grounding; cluster representations computed once but may shift with accumulating edits; max cluster size s_max=16 appears arbitrary; no comparison with alternative clustering approaches

Scalability limitations not adequately addressed: method requires storing m query representations (O(m·d) memory overhead); indexing becomes problematic at scale; acknowledged limitation of scaling to 'extra-large' knowledge bases but not addressed; true large-scale applicability (10K+ edits) unexplored

Safety and security analysis deferred despite being critical for knowledge editing: acknowledges risks (adversarial edits, bias amplification, robustness to biased policies) in Sec. 9 but defers investigation; concerning given knowledge editing's inherent modification of model behavior

Incomplete empirical validation: no statistical significance testing or error bars; results appear to be single runs; missing sensitivity to temperature parameter despite using extreme value (0.001); paraphrase generation method may introduce artifacts; routing accuracy under uncertainty near threshold not analyzed

Missing comparisons and ablations: no benchmarking against RAG approaches (mentioned but not compared); incomplete comparison with concurrent methods; different clustering strategies not explored; only 2 case studies in appendix; locality claims (1-1% MMLU drop) could use more detailed analysis

strengths: Strong empirical results demonstrating stable performance through 1,000 sequential edits while baselines degrade significantly (Table 1: 0.963 BERTScore on paraphrases vs 0.070-0.882 for baselines)
Well-motivated two geometric properties of LLM representations (Properties 1 and 2) with convincing empirical validation (Figure 1) forming solid foundation for the approach
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across multiple benchmarks (UnKEBench, EditEverything), models (LLaMA, Qwen), and baselines (7 different methods), with systematic ablations and analysis
Substantial practical improvements: 20% of baseline parameters (32.7M vs 180-293M) with 3× additional compression via shared-subspace training while maintaining utility (0.622 MMLU vs 0.633 baseline)
Thorough analysis including layer sensitivity (Figure 3), edit vector visualization (Figure 4), routing scalability (A.5), latency analysis (A.6), and cluster threshold ablations (A.7)
Practical system design: consistency-robust training for paraphrase generalization, query-adaptive routing for lifelong control, and shared-subspace intervention for memory efficiency
Qualitative case studies (A.8) convincingly demonstrate that RILKE produces coherent, correct outputs after 1,000 edits while baselines produce nonsensical or inaccurate outputs
weaknesses: Limited theoretical justification: geometric properties are empirically observed but lack explanation. Why do paraphrases concentrate in representation space? First-order Taylor expansion assumes small perturbations, but actual paraphrase distances may exceed this bound; Property 2 shows substantial scatter (R^l-similarity: 0.586-0.751)

Methodological concerns: (1) Using only last-token representation h^{l,i} for entire query is underexplored and may miss information for longer sequences; (2) Routing threshold 0.9 lacks ablation or principled justification; (3) Gaussian perturbation N(0,σ²I) choice not justified; (4) Multiple clustering hyperparameters (τ_sim, s_max, Δ) without principled selection guidance

Scalability limitations: (1) L2 distance routing is O(m·d) and could bottleneck at millions of edits; no timing analysis provided despite scalability claims; (2) Routing accuracy degrades with dataset size (Figure 6: 95%→85%); (3) Trade-off between memory and paraphrase generalization not thoroughly explored (Table 3: 0.963→0.901 BERTScore)

Limited generalization scope: (1) Evaluated only on 7-8B instruction-tuned models; unclear if mid-layer insights generalize to 70B+ models or base models; (2) Knowledge limited to factual/unstructured; behavioral and capability edits untested; (3) EditEverything paraphrases generated by Gemini (proprietary), not manually validated, raising reproducibility concerns

Statistical rigor issues: No confidence intervals, significance tests, or multi-run variance reported. Results appear to be single runs. Case studies (A.8) are qualitative cherry-picks without systematic evaluation

Key design choices lack ablation: Routing similarity threshold (0.9) never ablated; perturbation distribution choices not justified; sensitivity to σ and λ_robu not explored; layer selection requires manual tuning per model

Incomplete technical analysis: No discussion of failure modes or when method breaks down; conflict resolution in shared-subspace training for items with divergent edit targets unexplained; assumption that paraphrases activate same module even after large-scale editing needs validation

Reproducibility concerns: No code release mentioned; hyperparameter documentation incomplete (σ values, λ_robu, specific EasyEdit configurations); some critical implementation details scattered across appendix or missing
